manifest.hypothesis: Does a revocable fast-weight working memory improve recall of recent and updated facts within a session over a recency buffer and plain retrieval at an equal token budget? Operationalised: ptr_fastmem's gated delta-rule memory (FastMemory keyed by the projected frozen MiniLM embedding of a cue text, valued by the identifier code of the fact, beta 1 so an update replaces the association; decoded by decode_readout) is compared, on seeded synthetic sessions of 400 cues written, 200 of them updated later with a near-duplicate fact, and 400 paraphrased queries (160 about updated cues, 160 about never-updated cues, 40 about unwritten cues, 40 off-topic), with a recency buffer of the last 39 writes (floor(512 / 13) facts, answered by cosine on the frozen vectors) and with the pinned rag_reference hybrid retrieval (BM25 + cosine, RRF k=60) over the live facts (hybrid_live, gated) and over an append-only index (hybrid_append, reported). Every arm presents at most five facts within the 512-token budget and abstains at an operating point matched on pilot seeds (at most 5 percent of the unanswerable pilot queries answered). Update-aware recall@1 counts a query as right only when the arm's top fact is the current version of the queried cue; a false recall is a stale or other-cue top fact, or any answer to an unanswerable query. The memory must beat the recency buffer and hybrid_live in update-aware recall@1 (the lower bound of a paired bootstrap over the answerable queries of each seed must be positive) without a higher false recall rate than the recency buffer, its own contracts must hold (the product's decode equals the harness's independent decode, every write reads back through its own key, an exact-key overwrite leaves no stale association, the key projection binding refuses foreign queries), and no arm may exceed the token budget. The claim is scoped to this configuration: 400 cues written per session, the memory at 8 heads x key_dim 32 x value_dim 64 (shapes up to key_dim 384 appear only in the pilot), untrained seeded random projections of frozen MiniLM vectors, and a synthetic templated pool; descriptive evidence in every run (unthresholded recall, the cue text as the query, a threshold sweep and a capacity table over 16 to 400 cues) shows the regime in which the memory does and does not hold its cues. A negative result is a first-class outcome.

manifest.baseline: recency buffer of the last N facts (N = floor(token_budget / longest fact) = 39 of 512 tokens, answered by cosine on the frozen vectors); hybrid retrieval over the same facts (the Q003 stack: research/baselines/rag_reference BM25 + cosine, RRF k=60, over the live facts, frozen MiniLM vectors)
manifest.falsification: The run is vacuous and counts as falsified if any coverage prerequisite is unmet (but see the harness-integrity guards at the end of this list): updated_cue_queries < 100, unanswerable_queries < 50, old_stratum_queries < 100, written_facts < 500 (the generated session is too small); readback_checks < 500, stale_residual_checks < 100, projection_probes < 50 (fewer contract checks than required were made against the product); contract_probes < 80, contract_probe_margin_refusals < 20 (the decode contract probes on small memories of known readout were not made, or the ambiguous ones were not refused by margin; these are by construction); fast_score_abstentions < 20 (the score threshold was never reached by an organic query); unanswerable_answered_permille.fast, .recency or .hybrid_live > 150 (an arm is not at the matched operating point on this seed, so the comparison is vacuous); control_oracle_cheat_recall_permille < 1000, control_random_recall_permille > 100, control_stale_first_false_recall_permille < 300 (a negative control is not separated); control_positive_gain_vs_recency_lo_permille < 1, control_positive_gain_vs_hybrid_live_lo_permille < 1, control_positive_false_recall_headroom_permille < 0 (the positive control, the oracle-cheat answers standing in the memory's place and going through the same gain, bootstrap and false-recall path, does not pass the outcome rules: the pipeline cannot show a win; the harness also exits 2); oracle_label_mismatches > 0, stale_in_live_index > 0, window_budget_violations > 0 (harness and baseline integrity: the oracle's readings disagree, the live index returned a stale version, the recency window is over the budget; the aggregator judges a seed that trips any of these INVALID, not falsified). Falsified if any of: false_recall_fast_permille > false_recall_recency_permille (the memory's false recall rate over all queries is above the recency baseline's: the manifest's hard failure; a weak rule, since an arm that abstains almost always passes it); recall_gain_vs_recency_lo_permille < 1 or recall_gain_vs_hybrid_live_lo_permille < 1 (no gain in update-aware recall@1: the one-sided 95 percent paired-bootstrap lower bound of the memory's recall@1 minus the baseline's is not positive); token_budget_violations > 0 (an arm presented more than 512 tokens for one query); product_panics > 0, product_errors > 0 (the code under test panicked or refused a valid request, constructors included); stale_residual_violations > 0 (after an update the stale version still scores above the residual bound in a paraphrase-query readout); readback_failures > 0 (a write did not read back through its own key); decode_contract_violations > 0 (the product's decode differs from the harness's independent decode of the same readout, or returns an empty Hits); projection_mismatch_accepted > 0 (a query of another projection, or of none, was read by a projection-bound memory); any one of the 5 listed seeds misses any criterion above (every seed must pass). Descriptive and never judged: hybrid_append (every metric, the gain against it included), recall@k, the unthresholded recall of every arm, the memory's recall when asked with the cue text, the threshold sweep, the capacity table, unknown rates, tokens presented, the strata, latency_ns_per_query and every wall-clock time.
